issues.symptom: teardown platform hangs at 'envoy_ai_gateway | Uninstall CRDs Helm release' while a model's AIGatewayRoute still carries aigateway.envoyproxy.io/finalizer: the role strips finalizers only after the controller and the CRDs are gone
issues.workaround: k3d-gpu eas down sets the finalizers of every AIGatewayRoute to [] before it runs teardown platform --force (the issue's own workaround)

issues.symptom: model pods stay Pending on a node without feature.node.kubernetes.io/cpu-cpuid.AMXBF16=true: models.yaml defaults.require_amx is true and the renderer turns it into a required node affinity on that label
issues.workaround: eas-config.py writes defaults.require_amx to env/k3d-gpu/models.yaml from the nodes' AMXBF16 label (false without it)

issues.symptom: es_auto_installer.sh configure installs kubectl v1.34.3, three minors behind a k3d-gpu cluster's v1.37 API server, outside kubectl's supported skew of one minor
issues.workaround: the bastion bakes kubectl v1.37.2, the minor of the node image's K3S_TAG, and configure is never run

issues.symptom: with fs.inotify.max_user_instances at the kernel default of 128, file watchers in the stack's pods fail with 'too many open files'
issues.workaround: eas up warns below 8192 instances or 1048576 watches and prints the sysctl lines; the host is never changed

issues.symptom: the agent toolkit's documented minimum is 48 cores (96+ recommended); smaller nodes run it with less CPU for the model than the defaults assume
issues.workaround: eas up warns when the node has fewer than 48 allocatable CPUs

issues.symptom: the inference docs say './es_auto_installer.sh install inference --skip-models', but es_auto_installer.sh rejects any option it does not know ('Unknown option: --skip-models')
issues.workaround: none needed on the inference layer: EI's seeded config.yaml already sets llm_services_deploy_models: false. On the agent toolkit, EAT's chat model deploys whatever that key says; 'k3d-gpu eas up --agent-toolkit -- -e '{"llm_services_autodeploy_models": []}'' skips it (the guard model stays while the guardrail is on)

issues.symptom: keycloak_config runs kcadm.sh config credentials --password <admin password> and kcadm.sh update clients/<id> -s secret=<client secret> in the Keycloak pod through k8s_exec, so each value is in a process argv that ps lists on the node (on k3d, on the host) while the kcadm JVM runs; no_log hides it from Ansible's output only
issues.workaround: eas up applies patches/ei/0001-keycloak-config-kcadm-argv.patch (EI main) or its release-1.1 variant (EI v1.1.0) after init (ei-kcadm.sh): kcadm reads the password from KC_CLI_PASSWORD, copied in the pod from the operator's KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD, and Keycloak generates the client secret, which kcadm prints; the install stops when the task matches no variant. With auth_provider litellm (the agent toolkit at EAS v1.2.0) the role does not run. EI issue drafted, unsent (docs/intel/upstream-eat.md)

issues.symptom: redis_stack's validate runs redis-cli -a <Redis password> --no-auth-warning PING and MODULE LIST in the Redis pod through k8s_exec, so the password is in redis-cli's argv, which ps lists on the node (on k3d, on the host), for each call; no_log hides it from Ansible's output only
issues.workaround: eas.sh applies patches/eat/0001-redis-stack-validate-redis-cli-auth.patch after init and before each validate (eat-redis-cli.sh): redis-cli reads the password from REDISCLI_AUTH, copied in the pod from the REDIS_PASSWORD the chart sets from redis-stack-server-credentials; it stops when the task changed shape or another redis-cli call in EAT's roles, playbooks or charts passes the password as an argument. EAT issue drafted, unsent (docs/intel/upstream-eat.md)

issues.symptom: on k3s v1.37 (its gateway-api-crd addon installs Gateway API CRDs at v1.5.0 or later, with the safe-upgrades.gateway.networking.k8s.io ValidatingAdmissionPolicy), EAS v1.2.0's install stops at 'istio | Install Gateway API CRDs' (v1.2.1) and then at the gateway-helm install (its crds/ carry v1.4.1): 'Installing CRDs with version before v1.5.0 is prohibited by default'
issues.workaround: overlay rows 0007 and 0008 (integrations/eas/patches): the istio role applies its CRDs only when they are absent or older, and the envoy_gateway role keeps a Gateway API install at v1.5.0 or later, applying Envoy Gateway's own CRDs from gateway-crds-helm and installing the chart with skip_crds, as EAS main's gateway role does since EAS #42

issues.symptom: init <layer> writes the layer manifest's global_config: keys (auth_provider litellm for agent-toolkit) only into a global_config.yaml it creates; an env inited before (another layer, or EAS main, which had no such key) keeps its own with an info line, so install agent-toolkit runs without LiteLLM, its guardrail and the models' LiteLLM registration
issues.workaround: eas.sh sets the manifest's global_config: keys in env/k3d-gpu/global_config.yaml after init, and eas up refuses an env set up for another layer or other pins until eas down and --reset-env

issues.symptom: under the NRI balloons policy, a cpu: auto model takes one NUMA node's logical CPUs less EAS's reserve there and the balloon pods already placed; pods outside the balloons are not subtracted, so on a one-NUMA node whose reserve is small (one thread per core: 12 CPUs) the model leaves no room for EAT's sandbox router, which the toolkit installs after the models (H62: 'Insufficient cpu')
issues.workaround: eas-config.py estimates the auto value from the host's /sys topology and EAS's reserve and, when the pods outside the balloons would not fit beside it, writes an explicit cpu for the model in models.yaml (EAT's documented remedy)
